description: Per-character action index (plus ten mission/studio override rows) that binds a character to movement sub-tables and supplies the AttackSet IDs used by normal, cursed-energy, super and extra actions and by the command-list UI.

Id.simple: Row key, normally a CP_xxx/CN_xxx character ID; ten *_ST_* mission/studio override variants also exist.
Id.technical: FName in FGameDataTableRow_Action; the export labels the import key ID and its ImportKeyField is Id. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows selects ActionDataTables with GameCharacter_Override(Overrides.ActionIdOverride, CharacterDataTable.Id_Action) and fails when no row is found. MissionCharacterDataTable.Id_Action supplies that override in Story/Arcade/PvE setups; GameCommandListWidget instead resolves directly from CharacterDataTable.Id_Action.

Id_ActionMove.technical: FName into ActionMoveDataTables; required by ResolveDataRows and cached as AGameCharacter.ActionMoveRow (+0x3F0), which GetCurrentActionMoveRow uses only when the action controller has no override row. No studio override is applied. Shikigami movement resolves FGameDataTableRow_Shikigami.Id_ActionMove from ShikigamiDataTable, not this field.

Id_ActionJump.technical: FName into ActionJumpDataTables; required by ResolveDataRows and cached as AGameCharacter.ActionJumpRow (+0x3F8). No studio override is applied. Shikigami setup uses its own row struct's Id_ActionJump, not this field.

Id_ActionDash.technical: FName into ActionDashDataTables. FStudioBattleCharacterOverrides.ActionDashIdOverride, copied from MissionCharacterDataTable.Id_ActionDash by GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideIds in Story/Arcade/PvE setups, supersedes it when non-None; ResolveDataRows fails if neither resolves a row. Shikigami setup uses its own row struct's Id_ActionDash, not this field.

Id_ActionStep.technical: FName into ActionStepDataTables. Id_ActionBreakFall.technical: FName into ActionBreakFallDataTables; required by ResolveDataRows and cached as AGameCharacter.ActionBreakFallRow (+0x410). No override path was observed; all exported rows point to CP_010.

Id_AttackSet_CursedEnergy_1.simple: First grounded cursed-energy attack set, selected by level (index 3 is the finish-target set).
Id_AttackSet_CursedEnergy_1.technical: TArray<FName>; all 57 exported rows serialize exactly four entries. The generic finder maps controller cursed-energy level 1..3 to indices 0..2 and forces index 3 when the target is a finish target (not a level-4 case); it checks IsValidIndex and looks up the chosen FName in AttackSetDataTables with bCheckNone=true. None or an out-of-range index yields no set. Five rows populate index 3. The command-list UI also copies the first four entries for characters without a hardcoded exception.

Id_ExtraAttack_1.technical: FName into AttackSetDataTables resolved by character-specific ExtraAttack_1 actions in reconstructed CN_122, CN_230, CN_240, CN_250, CP_020, CP_050, CP_051, CP_070, CP_110, CP_170, CP_200, CP_230 and CP_270 (ground branch); CP_270 uses Id_ExtraAttack_2 for its air branch. None yields no set. The command-list extra-attack entries instead take Id_ExtraAttack_2 for both displayed slots.

notes: One exported table with 57 rows and 46 fields (38 FName scalars including Id and eight TArray<FName> fields); no numbered shards or localization variants for this group. Ten rows are *_ST_* mission/studio override variants referenced by MissionCharacterDataTable.

FGameDataTableRow_Action is an ABRAMSDATATABLE_API USTRUCT(BlueprintType) with all 46 fields BlueprintReadWrite/EditAnywhere. Its reconstructed constructor is empty and the header has no member initializers, so declared defaults are NAME_None / empty arrays; the shipped export instead serializes every field on all 57 rows, with all eight arrays exactly four entries long.

Override precedence is only for ActionIdOverride, ActionDashIdOverride and ActionStepIdOverride, and only a non-None override wins (GameCharacter_Override). Move, jump, break-fall and all AttackSet IDs have no studio override path; GameCommandListWidget also bypasses overrides by reading CharacterDataTable.Id_Action directly.

Cursed-energy array indices are 0..2 for levels 1..3 and 3 for a finish target, not level 4; five rows populate the finish index in each non-auto array. Several character overrides use alternate index sources or arrays (CP_220 charge-variant index, CP_070 airborne auto reads the ground CE1 array), so field names are not exclusive to one action class.

The command-list UI copies the first four cursed-energy entries unchecked except for hardcoded CP_030/CP_040/CP_060/CP_130/CP_230/CP_240 cases, then passes Id_AttackSet_SuperCursedEnergy and Id_ExtraAttack_2 directly to attack widgets.

UnknownSlot146 is a reconstructed, unproven name: its body returns SoloSide, otherwise true when no same-side character with CanHitAsAttacker is present or the Adapt_TagCombo stack is positive. Generic 1_1 actions use it, but CP_051 forces the solo ground field when its passive is absent and CP_121/CP_130 airborne overrides select the ground solo field.

Most normal _Auto fields are None in all 57 rows (1_Auto, Air_1_Auto, 1_1_Auto/Air_1_1_Auto and their Solo variants, 2_1_Auto/Air_2_1_Auto); populated cases are CP_090/CP_190 (2_Auto), CP_100/CP_230 (3_Auto) and CP_121/CP_220 (3_1_Auto). A None ID yields no set rather than falling back to the non-auto ID. No GetActionDamageRate override was found for generic normal _Auto classes; CE _Auto classes do return the owner auto-combo rate.

Action_FindAttackSetRow returns the first matching row in the manager's single AttackSetDataTables array or nullptr (None is rejected when bCheckNone=true); a null AttackSet with no Attack row makes FGameCharacterAction_AttackBase::Start abort. Some character actions cache the resolved row in HeldAttackSetRow for later chain hits.

Cross-table check against the read-only exports: every non-None movement ID resolves in the corresponding ActionMove/Jump/Dash/Step/BreakFall tables. 26 referenced AttackSet IDs (for example CP_010_ATTACKA_AIR and CN_090_ATTACKH_1) are absent from the available AttackSetDataTable export, so their shipped presence is not evidenced here.

Shipped evidence is the exported DataTable name/class/RowStruct/ImportKeyField and all row values; behavioral statements are from reconstructed C++ with retail RVAs in comments, not byte-match certificates. Available Content is partial, so unobserved Blueprint or retail-only uses are not excluded.

usages.detail: Resolves the Action row from CharacterDataTable.Id_Action or a non-None MissionCharacter-derived override, then resolves the five required movement sub-rows; a miss fails character setup.
Loads the single shipped ActionDataTable into ActionDataTables, the array used by all Action-row lookups.
Generic attack base uses Id_AttackSet_Normal_1 when no specialized action overrides it.
1_1 normal follow-up actions choose the solo or non-solo attack set via UnknownSlot146(); CP_051 uses its passive instead.
Cursed-energy actions index their four-entry arrays by controller level or finish-target index and look up the chosen ID in AttackSetDataTables.
Super attack actions resolve the grounded ID; character-specific airborne overrides sometimes read that ground field too.
Character-specific extra attack action resolves Id_ExtraAttack_1.
Character-specific extra attack action resolves Id_ExtraAttack_2.
One extra-attack action selects Id_ExtraAttack_1 on the ground and Id_ExtraAttack_2 in the air.
Command-list setup reads the Action row directly, copying four cursed-energy IDs and passing super/extra-2 IDs to display widgets.
AI conditions test the grounded super attack ID with IsNone before allowing super-attack behavior.
